- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect bearish sentiment’s reversal potential.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes; apply lagged smoothing: if price spiked, forecast next period should be slightly below peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above recent 5-10 day average, reduce by 5-10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-cycle momentum; if sentiment turns bullish mid-horizon, increase forecast slope toward end of period.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 or neutral readings, model tends to drift toward historical mean; apply mean-reversion correction if forecast deviates >1.5σ from recent 10-day average.
